name: Full Groom
summary: Bath, blow-dry, clip & style, nails & ears. The complete package.
heroPhotoAlt: Two golden retrievers looking fluffy after a full groom
metaDescription: Full dog grooming in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — bath, blow-dry, clip and style, nails and ears. Small from £40, medium £50, large or doodles £60.
body: A full groom is what most owners book and what most dogs need every six to eight weeks. It's the full dog grooming package: a careful pre-groom check, a warm bath with shampoo and conditioner matched to your dog's coat type, a thorough towel-and-blow-dry, a clip-and-scissor finish to whatever length you like, nails trimmed, ears cleaned and a final brush-out before your dog goes home.

Most full grooms take between one-and-a-half and three hours, depending on size and coat condition. I work at your dog's pace, not the clock's. There are no shared dryers, no other dogs in the room, and no rush to fit the next appointment in. A cockapoo who needs a break to sniff around the salon gets one.

If your dog hasn't been groomed in a long time, or the coat is heavily matted, the kindest thing is sometimes to clip down to a short, healthy length and let it grow back properly. I'll always talk you through it before we pick up the clippers, and I'll never carry on with a groom that's becoming stressful for your dog.

Pricing is by size and coat type: small dogs (terriers, shih-tzus, bichons) from £40, medium dogs (cockapoos, mini schnauzers, cocker spaniels) from £50, and large dogs or heavy-coated doodles (labradoodles, goldendoodles, retrievers) from £60. Heavy matting, anxious behaviour or unusually long gaps between grooms may sometimes add a little to the time and the price, I'll always confirm before we start.

What you do between grooms matters as much as the groom itself. A coat that is brushed regularly at home arrives in better shape, takes less time on the table, and is far less likely to need a shorter cut than you wanted. For curly and wavy coats (cockapoos, poodles, doodles) the brush needs to reach the skin, not skim the top — most home matting forms in the dense undercoat where a quick once-over never reaches. Line-brush in sections, lifting the coat and working from the skin outwards, paying extra attention to the friction points: behind the ears, under the collar or harness, the armpits, and the back legs. Five minutes most days beats half an hour once a week.

It helps to think about timing before you book. A coat clipped short will look its best for the first few weeks and then grow into the length you actually asked for, so if there is a date you want your dog looking sharp: a holiday, family photos, a show - book a week or two ahead rather than the day before. Smooth and short coats can stretch the interval; continuous-growth coats that never moult cannot, and pushing past the point where the coat starts to felt only moves cost from the groom to the de-matting session. If you are not sure where your dog sits, ask at the appointment and we will give you an honest interval for that specific coat.

There are a few things worth watching between visits, because catching them early keeps everything cheaper and kinder. A dog scratching at one ear, shaking the head, or a sour smell from the ear can mean it needs attention before the next groom. Nails clicking on a hard floor have grown long enough to affect how the dog stands. Tear staining that suddenly worsens, a paw being licked raw, or a patch of coat that mats again days after a groom are all worth a mention, sometimes it is the harness rubbing, sometimes it is skin that needs a vet rather than a groomer. We are happy to take a look and tell you honestly which it is.

faqs.q: How often should I book a full groom?
faqs.a: For most coats, every 6–8 weeks. Doodles and continuous-growth breeds (poodles, schnauzers, bichons) usually need 6 weeks; smoother coats can stretch to 8. Going much longer than 10 weeks risks matting that costs more to put right than the groom itself.

faqs.q: Do you do specific breed styles or lengths?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what you'd like!  A teddy-bear cockapoo, a schnauzer in breed standard, a shorter summer cut, and I'll work to it. I'll also flag honestly if your dog's coat or skin can't take what you've asked for.

faqs.q: What does the price actually include?
faqs.a: Bath with breed-appropriate shampoo, towel and blow-dry, full body clip and scissor finish, face and feet tidy, nail trim, ear clean and a final brush-out. Nothing's a hidden add-on.

faqs.q: Will my dog be on their own or with other dogs?
faqs.a: On their own. We only ever have one dog in the salon at a time. No kennels, no waiting.
